intro.caption: Lesson 5-8 — surface area of pyramids. The crew's desert expedition has one mission: coat the Golden Pyramid in gold leaf without running short!

balloons.t: Before we paint one cube, we need the pyramid's surface area so we pack enough gold!
Ooh, shiny blueprint! Just one tiny bite!
Easy! Use the straight-up vertical height inside the pyramid for the triangles!
Nope! That height is trapped inside! Each triangle face leans, so use its slant height.

pages.caption: The slant height runs right up the slanted triangular face—so it is the true height of each triangle.

balloons.t: Pick the slant height, then find the area of ONE triangular lateral face!
A square pyramid has four matching triangular lateral faces around the sides.
Find one triangle, then multiply by 4 to get the lateral area!
Look underneath, Dree! The pyramid sits on a flat square base.
Whoa! If we only add the four triangles, the whole bottom stays bare stone!
Bet you forget the base or mix up the heights like rookies!
Base plus four triangles—and we check when a base is open too!
340 square inches of gold! Not one cube missed!

win.caption: For a pyramid's surface area, add the base area plus all the triangular lateral faces—and always use the slant height for the triangles.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Choose the Slant Height
gates.prompt: Two heights are marked on the pyramid. Pick the slant height, then find one triangular face's area.
hints: Conceptual: the slant height lies right on the triangular face; vertical height goes straight up inside.
Procedural: use A = ½ × base edge × slant height for one triangle.

steps: Practice pyramid: base edge 6 in, vertical height 4 in, slant height 5 in.
Use the slant height (5 in) because it is the height of the triangle face.
worked.q: A pyramid has base edge 4 in and slant height 7 in. What is one triangle's area?

items.q: A square pyramid has base edge 8 in, vertical height 3 in, and slant height 5 in. Which height finds one triangular face's area?

options.t: Slant height (5 in), because it runs along the triangular face
Vertical height (3 in), because it goes straight up
options.fb: Vertical height is inside the pyramid, not on the slanted triangle face.

options.t: Base edge (8 in), because all sides are equal
options.fb: 8 in is the bottom edge (base) of the triangle, not its height.

items.label: Using base edge 8 in and slant height 5 in, area of ONE triangular face (in²):
items.aria: area of one triangular face in square inches

fb.msg: 40 is 8 × 5. A triangle is HALF of base × slant height!
12 uses the vertical height (½ × 8 × 3). Use the slant height 5 in.

gates.pass: Slant height 5 in, one face 20 in²! Dree puts the vertical ruler back in her pocket.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Lateral Area
gates.prompt: A square pyramid has 4 congruent triangular lateral faces. Find one face, then find all 4 together.
hints: Conceptual: lateral area means only the 4 side triangles, without the base.
Procedural: find one triangle with ½ × base × slant height, then multiply by 4.

steps: Practice pyramid: base edge 4 in, slant height 6 in.
worked.q: A square pyramid has base edge 5 in and slant height 8 in. What is its lateral area?

items.label: A square pyramid has base edge 10 in and slant height 9 in. Area of ONE triangle (in²):
items.aria: area of one triangle face for 10 by 9 pyramid

fb.msg: 90 is 10 × 9. Don't forget the ½ for a triangle!
19 is 10 + 9. Use ½ × base × slant height.

items.label: Total lateral area of all 4 triangular faces (in²):
items.aria: total lateral area of four triangular faces

fb.msg: 360 forgot the ½ on each triangle (4 × 90). Each triangle is 45 in².
45 is only 1 triangle. Multiply by 4 for all four lateral faces.
280 adds the 10 × 10 base! Lateral area is ONLY the 4 side triangles.

items.fbDefault: Multiply one triangle's area (45 in²) by 4.

gates.pass: 45 in² per face and 180 in² of lateral area! Moss mixes the gold leaf.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Add the Base
gates.prompt: Now include the square base! Find the base area, then add the 4 triangular faces for total surface area.
hints: Conceptual: total surface area = base area + lateral area.
Procedural: square base = side × side; add 4 × (½ × base × slant height).

steps: Practice pyramid: base edge 5 in, slant height 8 in.
Base area = 5 × 5 = 25 in². Lateral area = 4 × (½ × 5 × 8) = 80 in².
worked.q: A square pyramid has base edge 4 in and slant height 5 in. Total SA?

items.label: Square pyramid with base edge 6 in and slant height 8 in. Area of the square base (in²):
items.aria: area of 6 by 6 square base in square inches

fb.msg: 24 is the perimeter (6 × 4). Area of a square is side × side.

items.label: Add the 4 triangular faces (each ½ × 6 × 8) to the 36 in² base. Total SA (in²):
items.aria: total surface area of 6 by 6 base and slant height 8 pyramid

fb.msg: 96 is only the 4 triangles! Don't leave out the 36 in² square base.
60 only adds 1 triangle (36 + 24). There are 4 triangular faces.
228 forgot ½ on the triangles (36 + 4 × 48). Each triangle is ½ × 6 × 8 = 24.

gates.pass: 36 + 96 = 132 in²! Not a single bare stone left on the model.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Cover the Pyramid
gates.prompt: Cover the Giant Gold Pyramid (base 10 in, slant height 12 in), plus test an open-base glass display.
hints: Conceptual: include the base for total surface area; leave it out only when the problem says the base is open.
Procedural: SA = (side × side) + 4 × (½ × side × slant height).

steps: Practice pyramid: base edge 7 in, slant height 10 in.
worked.q: A square pyramid has base edge 8 in and slant height 9 in. Total SA?

items.label: Gold Pyramid: 10 in × 10 in base, slant height 12 in. Total surface area (in²):
items.aria: total surface area of 10 by 10 gold pyramid with slant height 12

fb.msg: 240 left out the 10 × 10 square base! Add 100 in² to the 240 in² of triangles.
580 forgot ½ on each triangle (100 + 4 × 120). Each triangle is ½ × 10 × 12 = 60.
160 only added 1 triangle (100 + 60). Multiply the triangle area by 4.

items.label: A glass display pyramid has base edge 3 ft, slant height 4 ft, and an OPEN base (no glass). Glass needed (ft²):
items.aria: glass needed for four triangular faces of open base pyramid

fb.msg: 33 added the 3 × 3 base, but the base is OPEN (no glass on the bottom).
48 forgot ½ on each triangle. Each triangle is ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 ft².
6 ft² is only 1 glass triangle. Multiply by 4 faces.

items.fbDefault: Skip the open base and compute 4 × (½ × 3 × 4).

items.q: When do you include the base area of a pyramid, and when do you leave it out?

options.fb: Total surface area includes every face, including the base.

options.t: Include the base for total surface area; leave it out only when the base is open
Always double the base like a prism
options.fb: A pyramid only has ONE base, not two.

gates.pass: SHINE! 340 in² of gold and 24 ft² of glass! The Champs drop their jaws as the pyramid glows.

journal.heading: Lesson 5-8 — what the pyramid raid taught us
rows: The height along a slanted triangular face. Always use slant height—never inside vertical height—for triangle area.
The total area of the triangular side faces only: 4 × (½ × base edge × slant height) for a square pyramid.
Base area + lateral area. Leave out the base only if the problem says the bottom is open.
Forgetting the base leaves the bottom bare, and using vertical height shrinks the triangles.
journal.quote: "Slant height for the sides, add the base at the bottom—unless it's open." — Ana

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 5-8 (Determine Surface Area of Pyramids) as one focused read. Covers only this lesson: distinguishing slant height from vertical height, finding lateral area of triangular faces, and adding the base area for total surface area.
standards: Find the surface area of right rectangular prisms, right triangular prisms, and pyramids using nets
